name: Biscayan Basque (Bizkaiera)

ancestors.notes: Biscayan shares the standard Basque grapheme inventory but diverges significantly in morphology and phonology; inherits grapheme-to-phoneme base from Batua.

notes: Biscayan (Bizkaiera/Bizkaia). Western Basque, spoken in Biscay and Araba. VALIDATED and CORRECTED against Bedialauneta Txurruka & Hualde (2023), an Illustration of the IPA of Markina Basque (a representative Biscayan variety). Key phonological features actually documented there: (1) MERGER of the apico-alveolar /s̺/ and lamino-alveolar /s̻/ fricatives in favour of a single apico-alveolar /s̺/, and of the affricates /ts̺/ and /ts̻/ in favour of a single denti-alveolar /ts̻/ (Bedialauneta & Hualde 2023: 1098) — so orthographic s and z both give /s̺/, and ts and tz both give /ts̻/; the standard three-way sibilant contrast of Batua is NOT present here. (2) MERGER of the voiceless palatal stop /c/ (spelled tt) with the postalveolar affricate /tʃ/, in favour of /tʃ/ (2023: 1098). (3) PALATALISATION after /i/: /s/→[ʃ] (haizea > /aiʃie/), /t/→[tʃ], /n/→[ɲ], /l/→[ʎ] (2023: 1102-1104). (4) NO aspiration: western Basque lost /h/ and has no aspirated stops (Hualde 2018: 2). (5) Voiced stops /b d ɡ/ are approximants [β ð ɣ] intervocalically and nasals assimilate in place to a following consonant (2023: 1099, 1103). Morphologically the most divergent dialect from Batua. NOTE (engine limit): the well-known Biscayan raising of the singular article /-a/ to [-e] after a high vowel (baso+a > basue, kale+a > kalie; Bedialauneta & Hualde 2023: 1107-1108) is a morphophonological process on the article, not a context-free grapheme rule, and is therefore not modelled at the orthography-to-IPA level. STRESS: the spec states "stress": false and does not take the Batua [+2] block of eu. Hualde (2022: 83, Table 1) lists the "Western-type accentual systems (with an accented vs unaccented contrast)" of Gernika-Getxo, Lekeitio, Markina, Ondarroa and Arratia. In them the unmarked words are unaccented and take a phrase-level accent ("Phrase-final accent" in Gernika-Getxo and Lekeitio, "Phrase-penultimate accent" in Markina, Ondarroa and Arratia), and each locality has its own rule for the accented exceptions. Hualde (2022: 83) also says that the Central systems, where all words are accented, include "varieties spoken in Bizkaia and Araba". The area therefore mixes phrase-level and word-level systems, the accented words are lexical, and the spelling marks neither. No single word-level block can be written from these sources.
